acceptConflict: Accept stopped: PR #{pr} conflicts with its target branch
acceptConflictDetail:
{url}
The conflict cannot be resolved by accepting: the code hosting service cannot merge this PR now. The platform hands the conflict to the AI teammate, which merges the target branch in the task directory, resolves it and pushes again. Accept again once the checks are green.
acceptDismissed: PR #{pr} has new commits; its existing approvals were dismissed
acceptDoneAfterReturn: PR #{pr} was merged on GitHub and the batch is closed; the earlier return stays on record
acceptDoneDetail:
{url}
The channel stays active; archiving it is a person's call. To deliver another change, create a new task.
acceptReady: PR #{pr} is ready to merge, waiting for {reviewer} to accept
acceptReadyDetail:
This PR meets the project's merge rules; accepting it merges it right away.
{url}
acceptStoppedMergeStateUnread: Could not read the merge state of PR #{pr}: {error}
acceptStoppedMergeUnconfirmed: The merge result of PR #{pr} cannot be confirmed yet; retry to check the repository's state
acceptStoppedNoCommits: Accept not completed: the branch has no commits
acceptStoppedNoCommitsDetail: The change under review is “{subject}”, but branch {branch} has no commits, so there is no PR to open and nothing to merge. The change may be on another branch; push it to {branch} and accept again.
acceptStoppedNoCredentials: Could not get the platform's GitHub authorization ({why})
acceptStoppedPrClosed: PR #{pr} was closed on GitHub without being merged
acceptStoppedPrOpenFailed: Accept not completed: the PR could not be opened
acceptStoppedPrOpenFailedDetail:
{reason}.
The platform will not push a change upstream without a PR. Retry the accept once this is sorted out.
acceptStoppedPrStalled: PR #{pr} cannot move forward right now
acceptStoppedPrUnavailable: Accept not completed: the PR could not be merged
acceptStoppedPrUnavailableDetail:
{why}.
A project bound to GitHub is accepted only by merging its PR; the platform will not bypass the PR and push upstream directly. Retry the accept once this is sorted out.
acceptStoppedTitleDisagrees: PR #{pr}'s title on GitHub differs from the title it was submitted for review with; the accept is paused
acceptStoppedStatusUnread: Could not read the status of PR #{pr}: {error}
archiveStoppedFollowing: The channel was archived; the platform stopped following PR #{pr}
archiveStoppedFollowingDetail:
{url}
This PR is not merged. The platform will not close it; someone needs to decide whether to close it.
artifactDeclared: This delivery created a new artifact, “{name}”, which the project did not have before
cardRedescribed: {actor} edited the review description (synced to the PR)
cardFocusUpdated: {actor} edited what the review asks to check
cardRedelivered: {actor} replaced what is under review; earlier approvals were cleared and it needs another look
cardRejectedClosed: {who} sent the changes back; the original task is closed
cardRejectedFixing: {who} sent the changes back; they are being revised
cardVoidedDetail: Voided in state “{state}”. This is not a return and does not mean the checks failed; it only ends this review so the channel can submit again.{reason}
checksPassed: Checks on PR #{pr} are all green; it can be submitted for review now
checksPassedAwaitingReview: Checks on PR #{pr} are all green; waiting for review
dependencyActionDelivered: The target branch is now {branch}. Fetch the remote branch, rebase this task's commits onto it, resolve conflicts, rerun the checks and push. The parent may have been squash-merged, so check the patches and replay only this task's own changes; do not bring back ancestor changes the parent dropped and that have not been approved again. A clean rebase does not prove the commit range is right; check that the final diff contains only this task's delivery.
dependencyActionUndelivered: Keep the existing work and check which undelivered changes this task depends on. Following the task's requirements, decide whether to drop the dependency, implement it independently, or report why you cannot continue; do not treat a rejection or a close as merged code, and do not close the subtask automatically. To drop the dependency, rebuild this task's own commits on its branch with the project's default branch as the base, verify the diff contains none of the rejected changes, then run cheese push-fix --drop-dependency. It retargets the existing PR, clears the task dependency and old approvals; do not file the card again or merge it yourself.
dependencyHeadline: The parent task {outcome}; this subtask needs to recheck its dependencies
dependencyHistory:
Past rejections of ancestor dependencies follow. They are not the current state: read the review cards and tasks again to check which changes were withdrawn or approved later.
{items}
dependencyHistoryItem:
Past rejection reason on review card {card}:
{reason}
dependencyOutcomeReturned: was sent back and is still in progress
dependencyRejection: The parent task's latest review card {card} was rejected. {why}
forceMergedVerdictFailure: Merged knowing the checks were not all green
forceMergedVerdictNoChecks: No CI had run on this change at the time
forceMergedVerdictOther: The check status at the time was {state}
forceMergedVerdictPending: Merged without waiting for the checks to finish
forceMergedVerdictSuccess: The checks were in fact all green at the time
forceMergedVerdictUnread: The check status could not be read at the time
gateAbandoned: Check result lost; the review was ended
gateAbandonedNudge:
Check incomplete: the review you submitted got stuck in the platform's quality check. The platform never got the check result (the backend restarted or the check task was lost), so it ended the review; nobody will receive it.

**This is not a failed check**: the check never finished, and nothing shows your code has a problem, so there is nothing to fix. Make sure the workspace is still as you delivered it, then **submit the review again**.
gateCondemned: Check incomplete; the review was ended
gateCondemnedDetail:
The platform could not get this check's result, usually because the check task was lost when the backend restarted.
This is not a failed check: the check did not finish, and nothing shows the code has a problem. Just submit the review again.
mergeQueueLeft: PR #{pr} left the merge queue without merging
mergeRefusedOnAccept: Accept not completed: GitHub refused to merge PR #{pr}
mergeWithheld: The platform will not merge PR #{pr} automatically
mergeWithheldBehind: The branch keeps falling behind main (still behind after 3 automatic rebases); main may be moving too fast or the rebase is not taking effect, so a person needs to handle it
mergeWithheldBehindWhy: The platform's automatic branch updates cannot keep up with main.
mergeWithheldCheckMissing: The required check {checks} has never run (waited more than {minutes} minutes); the workflow may not have triggered, or was renamed or disabled, and the platform will not decide on anyone's behalf that it can be skipped
mergeWithheldCheckMissingWhy: The check did not fail; it never reported at all. The platform can only confirm that nobody ran it, not decide for anyone that it need not run.
mergeWithheldVotes: Set to merge once checks pass, but there are not enough approvals ({votes}/{required})
mergeWithheldVotesWhy: The rules are met, but the vote of the person who set it to merge on its own does not reach the number of approvals the project requires.
migrationCollision: Another change awaiting review also adds a database migration
migrationCollisionDetail:
The other change is in: {rooms}.
Each change carries its own alembic revision; once both merge, the migration chain forks, which usually also means the same thing was done twice.
The platform will not block this accept. Compare the two changes first: if they really are two different things, accept as usual, and after the first one merges the other needs a rebase.
prClosed: PR #{pr} was closed without merging; the review is void
prClosedDetail:
The PR was closed on GitHub without being merged, so the platform voided this review and will not merge it. To keep delivering, submit a new review.
{url}
prConflict: PR #{pr} conflicts with its target branch
prMergedDelivered: PR #{pr} was merged in the repository; the task is delivered
prMergedExternally: was merged by hand on GitHub (not by the platform)
prReviewCapped: Review on PR #{pr} has gone back and forth {limit} times; a person needs to step in
prTitleDisagrees: PR #{pr}'s title on GitHub differs from the title it was submitted for review with; merging is paused
taskStepLanded: This delivery of “{title}” was accepted · PR #{pr}; the task goes on
taskStepLandedNoPr: This delivery of “{title}” was accepted; the task goes on
taskClosedUndelivered: “{title}” was accepted, but work still going on in it had not finished past the deadline: the task is closed, and that work was stopped without being delivered
mainChecksFailed: Checks failed after merge: {checks}. {agent} will fix them in this step
mainChecksFailedReopened: Checks failed after merge: {checks}. The task is reopened for {agent} to fix
